translations.answer: Confirm whether the constraint is written as an equality only dependent on state; community suggests rewriting it as a state-input equality and avoiding hard-penalizing residual errors. When gradient calculations are large, evaluate the analytical derivative of Pinocchio.
translations.applicability: Applicable to OCS2 full-body NMPC using q and ν as state and SQP solver; other solvers need to re-verify constraint support.
translations.credibility.rationale: Engineering records exist for environment, processing steps and results, but formal cross-validation or independent replication is missing.
translations.details.attempts.0: Original author tried constraint observer and penalty methods, but slipping still exists.
translations.details.diagnostics.0: Distinguish between pure-state equality constraints and state-input equality constraints, then verify SQP solver support range.
translations.details.effective_fixes.0: Community suggests changing the constraint to the acceleration layer's end, making it a state-input equality constraint.
translations.details.environments.0: OCS2, Pinocchio, full-body NMPC, state is q and ν, input is ground reaction force and joint torque.
translations.details.limits.0: Conclusion is based on community practice; response also states the judgment on OCS2 SQP capability is based on previous version, should re-check current version.
translations.details.outcomes.0: Response provides direction for re-implementation, but original author did not post final experimental results in the Issue.
translations.details.problem_statements.0: Support foot zero velocity constraint is violated during standing and small running.
translations.details.safety_notes.0: Before real machine testing, check foot end constraint residuals and friction margin to avoid bringing simulation slippage into hardware.
translations.details.suspected_causes.0: Writing the foot zero velocity as a pure-state equality constraint, but the solver path cannot directly handle it.
translations.details.symptoms.0: Support foot continues to slip, some runs directly crash.
translations.media_summaries.0: Issue includes screenshot of foot end constraint observer and slippage video; this round only confirms the phenomenon based on the author's text description, and specific numerical values have not been pixel-by-pixel verified.
